summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of COPD, chronic DVT/PE, atrial myxoma, and chronic pain was admitted for worsening dyspnea over two months, despite multiple prior hospitalizations and prolonged steroid use. Workup revealed no acute pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, or cardiac ischemia. Imaging showed a new stenosis in the left pulmonary artery and a VQ scan with a perfusion-ventilation mismatch, findings suggestive of chronic thromboembolic disease but not requiring urgent intervention. Hemoptysis was noted but deemed likely due to coughing on anticoagulation. The patient exhibited behavioral patterns raising concern for secondary gain and opioid misuse, including inconsistent symptom reporting and a history of multiple prescribers. He was maintained on home medications with an increased dose of inhaled corticosteroid, and opioids were withheld due to safety concerns. He remained stable, with no further bleeding or respiratory decline, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged and strong recommendations to continue anticoagulation and engage in longitudinal care.
